title: Industrial Engineering Intern
summary: I work across the factory floor and the data behind it—building tools that make manufacturing information visible, useful, and actionable.
bullets: Developed a connected digital pressure-testing and reporting system — Raspberry Pi operator stations, live pressure capture, guided three-pop/bubble-test workflows, centralized test records, and a manager dashboard — with a planning-level estimate of ~1,453 labor-hours/year recoverable across testing, documentation, and administrative work.

Analyzed two years of production data and modeled the facility in AutoCAD (104 activity locations, 10,816 origin-destination travel paths) to identify material-flow improvements, producing a recommended future state with an estimated 18.75% reduction in modeled transportation effort and roughly a one-year planning-level payback.

Built a Python application (the Valve Decoder) that converted 19,567 historical shipped-valve records and 1,951 unique valve models from hard-to-use PDF pick-sheets into a structured, searchable database — used to close data gaps in the facility flow study and since expanded into a reusable engineering reference tool.
